items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: somebody like Wilbur Dinkle, Adam Bound.

ctx.x: I became a member, let me think now, I guess it would have been about 19, about 27. I'd have to look that up myself. The union at that time was on Royal Street in the 300 block, roughly about 305, something like that, on the second or third floor. And I heard about a drive they were having for new members in which the initiation fee was lowered to $15. And so a whole raft of us went in, because in those days, you weren't considered a professional musician unless you were in the union. Because all the guys who…

would tell you, I think you're ready for the union. Yeah, well, the prelude was too joint, you know. Yes. We got preludes from somebody, I can't remember who, somebody like Wilbur Dinkle, Adam Bound. My goodness, that's a good name. Yeah. Well, those guys, obviously they took pride in things. Oh, completely. Save those, save those, every fragility. You mentioned Wilbur Dinkle. Let me

get into one of my famous deviations. Wilbur had the job at the Old Dauphine Theater, which was a burlesque house, and Fazola used to play there with him too. I guess you know that somewhere along the line too. No, I don't remember that. Oh, yes. Oh, yes. They had about a six-piece band to play for the strippers on stage in the comics, and Faz was, he played Wilbur Dinkle. In fact, they were, let's say, drinking partners. They liked to go out together at night. And this was before Faz went off. You know, he was…
